nonStandardPatterns.whatItDoes: The per-result 'Select' control. It is a real form submit button styled to look like a link; submitting posts add-id=<establishment UUID> and navigates to establishment-of-origin. Each logical establishment is rendered once in the desktop form and again in the mobile form, so the observed 10 results produce 20 Select buttons.
nonStandardPatterns.concern: Custom 'link-button' class, not a Design System component. A button dressed as a link is an accessibility/consistency smell. The dual render also duplicates ids select-establishment-1 through select-establishment-10 in the same DOM.
nonStandardPatterns.govukAlternative: Use a standard govuk-button (or govuk-button--secondary) per row, or a genuine link if the action is navigational; keep the submit semantics.
nonStandardPatterns.evidence: trace 94d29a163f6ab37556cd585b4eabeec9b9c27d84 action 57 before snapshot (20 button[name='add-id'] controls: 10 under .establishments-search-results-form-desktop and 10 under .establishments-search-results-form-mobile; ids 1-10 are repeated)

nonStandardPatterns.pattern: pagination / pagination-list / pagination-item / pagination-item-next / pagination-link / pagination-link-icon / pagination-link-label / pagination-link-title
nonStandardPatterns.whatItDoes: Bespoke pagination widget rendering 'Next page : 2 of 5' with a link to ?establishment-country-code=AF&page=2.
nonStandardPatterns.concern: Entirely custom pagination markup — does NOT use the GOV.UK Pagination component.
nonStandardPatterns.govukAlternative: GOV.UK Pagination component (govuk-pagination) covers previous/next and numbered pages out of the box.

nonStandardPatterns.whatItDoes: Dual-renders the results: a govuk-table for desktop and a stacked card list (H3 govuk-label--s field headings + P values per establishment) for mobile, toggled by responsive classes. Each form also repeats its crumb, etag and ten add-id submit controls.
nonStandardPatterns.concern: Custom responsive dual-render of the same data. GOV.UK tables do not natively transform to mobile cards; two parallel DOM structures increase maintenance and a11y risk, including duplicated Select-control ids.
nonStandardPatterns.govukAlternative: A single responsive govuk-table, or the community responsive-table pattern, rather than two separate rendered structures.
nonStandardPatterns.evidence: trace 94d29a163f6ab37556cd585b4eabeec9b9c27d84 action 57 before snapshot (desktop and mobile form class inventory; each contains 10 add-id buttons and hidden crumb/etag inputs)

nonStandardPatterns.whatItDoes: Custom wrapper classes around the filter panel and results table for IPAFFS-specific layout/styling.
nonStandardPatterns.concern: IPAFFS-specific styling hooks; not part of the Design System. Low risk but should map to govuk grid/spacing utilities in the rebuild.
nonStandardPatterns.govukAlternative: govuk-grid + govuk spacing utilities; no bespoke panel class needed.

fields.name: establishment-country-code
fields.label: Country (required)
fields.requiredEvidence: Not mandatory in the authorised search handler despite the legacy label saying '(required)': getSearchParameters adds countryCode only when establishment-country-code is present, and the GET performs the search without a page validator (ipaffs-frontend-notification/service/src/routes/handlers/importer/veterinary_establishments.js:28-52,83-98). The select also has no null prompt in the template, so normal UI submission supplies its current option (service/src/views/importer/veterinaryEstablishments.html:32-42). This legacy copy/behaviour discrepancy should be resolved for the rebuild.
fields.evidence: trace 94d29a163f6ab37556cd585b4eabeec9b9c27d84 action 57; also trace 07531e0d159b90b8ecddb13cf441bda4c493d68b action 55. Full country reference list (251 options), pre-selected to the notification's country of origin (suffixed '(country of origin)'), ends with 'Not Found'. Reference data — the new app must source it from a reference-data service, not hardcode. Note: label reads '(required)' but the <select> has no HTML required attribute. page-objects/notification/SearchForApprovedEstablishmentPage.ts:10-16 exposes the Country (required) selector and Search button; workflows/notification/ched-p-workflows.ts:374-382 selects the configured establishment country before searching for additional establishments; tests/accessibility/ched-p-accessibility-tests.spec.ts:111-120 selects France, searches, and then selects a result; types/country.ts:2 and types/country.ts:80 define the QA values AF and FR.

fields.name: add-id
fields.label: Select
fields.requiredEvidence: Conditionally mandatory to complete the selection action: each result button submits add-id containing the establishment UUID (ipaffs-frontend-notification/service/src/views/partials/importer/establishmentSearchDesktop.html:50-55; service/src/views/partials/importer/establishmentSearchMobile.html:64-68), and the POST handler immediately reads that value and retrieves the approved establishment (service/src/routes/handlers/importer/veterinary_establishments.js:55-74). The persisted establishmentsOfOrigin list is @NotEmpty for NotificationVeterinaryApprovedEstablishmentValidation (ipaffs-imports-notification-schema/notification-schema-java/src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/tracesx/notificationschema/representation/VeterinaryInformation.java:32-37). It is not required merely to run or refine a search.
fields.conditionalOn: Rendered twice per logical approved-establishment result: once in the desktop results form and once in the mobile results form. The observed page has 10 establishments and 20 add-id buttons.
fields.evidence: trace 94d29a163f6ab37556cd585b4eabeec9b9c27d84 action 57 before snapshot. Submit buttons name='add-id', value=establishment UUID; clicking one selects that establishment and navigates to establishment-of-origin. Rendered as class 'link-button' (see nonStandardPatterns). The same ten UUIDs and ids select-establishment-1 through select-establishment-10 occur in both desktop and mobile forms, producing 20 DOM controls for 10 logical results. page-objects/notification/SearchForApprovedEstablishmentPage.ts:22-27 and page-objects/notification/SearchForApprovedEstablishmentPage.ts:34-47 independently identify the row Select button and use it to select the first result; page-objects/notification/SearchForApprovedEstablishmentPage.ts:50-81 traverses Next-page pagination when necessary to select a distinct result; workflows/notification/ched-p-workflows.ts:369-385 uses this behaviour for one or more approved establishments; tests/notification/ched-p/ched-p-notification.spec.ts:307-313 proves a RoW CHED-P journey can complete with 10 approved establishments.

validationMessages.trigger: No applicable legacy validation: Search is submitted without an establishment-country-code query parameter
validationMessages.evidence: The authorised GET handler has no page validator and conditionally adds countryCode only when the query parameter is present, so there is no legacy country-required error copy even though the label says '(required)' (ipaffs-frontend-notification/service/src/routes/handlers/importer/veterinary_establishments.js:28-52,83-98; service/src/views/importer/veterinaryEstablishments.html:32-42).

validationMessages.message: No establishments have been found. Re-try by amending your search criteria.
validationMessages.evidence: Verbatim authorised empty-results copy, rendered in both the desktop results row and mobile results card when pageResults is empty after a search (ipaffs-frontend-notification/service/src/views/partials/importer/establishmentSearchDesktop.html:58-67; service/src/views/partials/importer/establishmentSearchMobile.html:75-87).

validationMessages.trigger: CHED-P approved-establishment validation runs while no approved establishment has been selected
validationMessages.evidence: Verbatim model-validation copy in ValidationMessages.properties, used by the @NotEmpty establishmentsOfOrigin constraint for NotificationVeterinaryApprovedEstablishmentValidation (ipaffs-notification-microservice/service/src/main/resources/ValidationMessages.properties:142; ipaffs-imports-notification-schema/notification-schema-java/src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/tracesx/notificationschema/representation/VeterinaryInformation.java:32-37). Selecting add-id is what appends the chosen establishment to that list (ipaffs-frontend-notification/service/src/transformers/view_to_notification/importer/veterinary_establishments.js:3-18).

openQuestions: Results-table columns (Name, Section, Type, Approval Number, Status, Country, Select) and per-row data are trace-confirmed, but neither the traces nor the QA page object exercise the Name/Approval-number free-text filters, Section/Type/Status dropdowns, or Sort control. The QA page object only exposes Country, Search, row selection and pagination (page-objects/notification/SearchForApprovedEstablishmentPage.ts:10-31). Their filtering/sorting behaviour and validation remain gaps.

No error/validation states were captured in the traces. The authorised legacy source resolves the behaviour: no-results renders "No establishments have been found. Re-try by amending your search criteria.", while country has no server-side required rule even though its label says "Country (required)" (ipaffs-frontend-notification/service/src/views/partials/importer/establishmentSearchDesktop.html:58-67; service/src/routes/handlers/importer/veterinary_establishments.js:28-52,83-98). Confirm whether the rebuild should make Country genuinely required or remove '(required)' from the label.

The country select is pre-selected to the notification's country of origin ('Afghanistan (country of origin)'); whether the user can freely change country to search other countries' establishments, and how 'country of origin' is derived, is inferred not confirmed.
Pagination shows 10 results per page and 'Next page : 2 of 5'; total-count / previous-page / numbered-page rendering was not exercised.

Above the main region a notification-reference banner renders 'DRAFT.GB.2026.1525975 - CHEDP' (govuk-caption-l style, outside <main>) and a 'Back' link with href='#'. Treated as chrome; the Back target is JS-driven and its destination was not traced.

The Section and Type reference lists contain obvious data-quality duplicates (e.g. two near-identical 'Blood and blood products...' entries, 'Frogs legs' vs "Frogs' legs"). The rebuild should dedupe/canonicalise this reference data at source.
